summary:
Round 5, scoped to the one assertion added to LogKeysTest.aKeyTooSHORTToCarryTheGrammarIsRefusedRatherThanThrowing since 6e889cf0920b. VERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT, not by reading. The new assertion passes on the unmutated tree (742/742 green) and is the UNIQUE killer of the whole suffix-narrowing family: endsWith(SUFFIX) narrowed to "delta", "elta", "lta", "ta", "a" or "" -- every proper suffix of ".delta" -- each leaves all four writer-produced keys passing and each makes <logPrefix>delta slice substring(32,31). Two of these were run through the real suite under Gradle (endsWith("delta") and endsWith("a")): each produced exactly ONE failure across all 742 tests, and it was this assertion. My round-4 T3 finding is CLOSED. It makes no existing assertion break; it does subsume KEYS.logPrefix()+"x", which now has no unique kill in any mutant I could construct -- that is redundancy, not weakness, and I am not asking for it to be removed. I hunted for a further survivor as instructed and found no NEW dangerous one: the two remaining survivors on isEntryKey are argued equivalent, and the grammar-level mutations (SUFFIX -> "delta", unpadded %016x) are both killed by CommitLogTest and IngestCommitPathTest, measured. T4 and T5 are unchanged by the addition. The new comment's factual claims are all true as measured. One pre-existing comment on the assertion above it is false; it is out of the delta, it is a minor, and it should be RECORDED rather than fixed -- fixing it buys another round for another paragraph to be wrong in, which is the exact failure this task's own baseline entry records. No assertion was weakened anywhere in the delta: the hunk is +6 lines with zero removals (testing.md rules 4-5 satisfied). Review tree restored; repository staged diff unchanged at 132bf9c19978a1 and ./gradlew test green.

MEASUREMENT RECORD (evidence, not findings -- the schema has no `info` severity and I will not inflate evidence into minors):

* [T3-CLOSED] sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/LogKeysTest.java:92-97 -- The round-4 T3 survivor is dead, and the kill is unique
  MEASURED under Gradle in an isolated tree, full suite each time. Mutation A: `!key.endsWith(SUFFIX)` -> `!key.endsWith("delta")` in LogKeys.isEntryKey -- 742 tests, 1 failure, LogKeysTest.aKeyTooSHORTToCarryTheGrammarIsRefusedRatherThanThrowing, StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: Range [32, 31) out of bounds for length 37. Mutation B: `!key.endsWith("a")` -- identical result, same single failure, same range. Length 37 = logPrefix(32) + "delta"(5), i.e. the new assertion and nothing else. Before it was added both mutants were green across the whole suite. I then enumerated the family exhaustively against a faithful model of isEntryKey (validated against the four Gradle runs, exception ranges matching exactly): the narrowed operand "delta", "elta", "lta", "ta", "a" and "" (i.e. dropping the guard) are ALL killed by this one case, and by this case alone for the first five. The guard's operand is now pinned, not merely its presence.

* [T-R5-1] sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/LogKeysTest.java:81-83 -- Per-assertion kill matrix: the new case subsumes `logPrefix() + "x"`, which now has no unique kill
  Re-derived because that was the only way to be sure. Kill attribution across the four assertions in this method (A1=".delta", A2=logPrefix+"x", A3="bins.delta", A4=logPrefix+"delta"), each mutation applied alone: endsWith narrowed to any proper suffix of ".delta" -> killed by A4 ONLY. endsWith guard dropped entirely -> killed by A2 and A4 (A2 fires first, Range [32,27) length 33; A4 would fire if A2 were deleted). startsWith(logPrefix) -> startsWith(prefix) -> killed by A3 ONLY, Range [32,4) length 10. startsWith guard dropped -> killed by A1 and A3 (A1 fires first, Range [32,0) length 6; A3 alone suffices). `||` -> `&&` -> killed by all four. The first three Gradle runs confirm the model's exception ranges exactly. CONSEQUENCE: A3 and A4 each carry a unique kill; A1 and A2 do not -- A2's only kill is the guard-deletion mutant that A4 also kills, and A1's only kill is the one A3 also kills. Nothing is broken by the addition and I am NOT asking for a deletion: an assertion that names the guard it pins is documentation as well as a kill, and deleting one under non-negotiable 2 would need a better reason than economy. Recorded so a later reader knows the matrix rather than guessing it.

* [T-R5-2] sequencer/src/main/java/binjava/sequencer/LogKeys.java:74 -- I treated 'one more survivor exists' as the default and looked; the two that survive are argued equivalent, and the grammar mutations are killed elsewhere
  Eighteen mutants of isEntryKey enumerated and scored; five run through the full Gradle suite. SURVIVORS: (1) `endsWith(SUFFIX)` -> `contains(SUFFIX)` -- 742 tests, 0 failures. It is equivalent for the RETURN VALUE unconditionally, because the final `key.equals(keyFor(sequence))` admits only the canonical key, which ends in ".delta" by construction; and it cannot throw for any key this code is ever handed, because logPrefix contains no '.', so a ".delta" match starts at index >= logPrefix.length() and forces key.length() >= logPrefix.length()+6. NOTE the one condition on that argument: it holds because the configured `prefix` contains no ".delta". With prefix="a.delta" the mutant throws on <logPrefix>x. That is a hypothetical about a configuration value, not a live hazard, and I am not asking for a test. (2) `key.equals(keyFor(seq))` -> `keyFor(seq).equals(key)` -- equivalent, both operands non-null. (3) narrowing startsWith to any LONGER proper prefix of logPrefix (e.g. dropping the trailing '/') survives, and unlike the endsWith case it is production-unreachable: both call sites feed isEntryKey the results of store.list(logPrefix, ...), so every key reaching it already starts with the full logPrefix. That asymmetry is exactly why the endsWith operand needed pinning and the startsWith operand needed it less -- the new comment's word 'asymmetry' is right for a reason it does not state. KILLED, measured, and therefore NOT gaps: SUFFIX ".delta" -> "delta" fails CommitLogTest.theKeyCarriesTheEpochZeroPaddedSoLexicographicOrderIsNumericOrder; logPrefix "%016x" -> "%x" fails that test plus epochPrefixesSortInNumericOrderAcrossTheNineToSixteenBoundary and IngestCommitPathTest. The grammar this commit MOVED into LogKeys is pinned outside it.

* [T-R5-3] sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/LogKeysTest.java:92-97 -- The new comment and its `.as` description are both true, checked clause by clause
  "narrowing endsWith(SUFFIX) to endsWith(\"delta\") -- or any suffix of it": the suffixes of "delta" are delta/elta/lta/ta/a/"", and all six are covered -- TRUE. "leaves every real key passing": keyFor(0), keyFor(9), keyFor(16), keyFor(Long.MAX_VALUE) all still return true under all six -- TRUE, measured. "and this one slicing backwards": Range [32, 31), measured under Gradle -- TRUE. The `.as` text "ends with a proper suffix of \".delta\"": <logPrefix>delta ends with "delta", which is a proper suffix of ".delta" -- TRUE, and it does NOT end with ".delta" itself, so it is not ambiguous. Nothing in the added prose is false. Raised as info because this project's baselines record false claims inside fixes for previous findings as a recurring failure, so 'I checked it and it holds' is worth stating rather than leaving silent.

* [T-R5-5] sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/LogKeysTest.java:1 -- T4 and T5 are unchanged by the addition; testing.md rules 4-5 satisfied; tier is right
  T4 (isEntryKey(".delta") has no unique kill): still true -- its only kill, dropping the startsWith guard, is also killed by "bins.delta". The new assertion neither creates nor removes a unique kill for it. T5 (three equivalent mutants argued): unchanged -- the new assertion kills none of them, and the equivalence arguments do not depend on it. RULES 4-5: the delta on this file is a single +6 hunk with zero deletions and zero modified lines; no existing assertion was loosened, disabled or deleted alongside the production change. TIER: LogKeysTest is T0 throughout -- a record with two fields, no socket, no clock, no store, no sleep, no fixed port, no system temp. Non-negotiable 7 is satisfied by construction here, and that is the point of the LogKeys split: the naming question is answerable without a writer.

findings.title: PRE-EXISTING, OUT OF DELTA: the comment above the `bins.delta` assertion states a false reason -- record it, do not fix it this round
findings.detail: "The two cases above miss it, since neither starts with `bins` either." One of the two, KEYS.logPrefix() + "x", IS "bins/ctl/log/0/0000000000000001/x" and DOES start with "bins". Under startsWith(logPrefix) -> startsWith(prefix) it passes the startsWith guard and is refused one step later by the endsWith guard, so it misses the mutant for the opposite reason to the one stated. Only ".delta" misses it for the stated reason. The assertion itself is correct and uniquely kills that mutant -- measured, Range [32,4) length 10 -- so nothing about the coverage is wrong; only the explanation is. This text was in the tree at 6e889cf0920b and already carries a verdict, and review.md's round accounting says a minor on a pass LANDS. ⚠️ MY RECOMMENDATION IS EXPLICITLY NOT TO FIX IT NOW: this task has already spent a round on a comment, the surface of a fix is the prose the fix adds, and this file's own history is a comment being wrong inside the fix for the previous comment being wrong. Carry it in the commit body or a backlog row.
findings.failure_scenario: A later session reads this comment to decide what the `bins.delta` case is for, believes the stated reason -- that the other two cases miss the startsWith-narrowing mutant because they do not start with `bins` -- and generalises it into the next filter test: it adds a case that merely avoids the configured prefix and believes that pins the guard's operand. It does not. `KEYS.logPrefix() + "x"` DOES start with `bins`; it misses that mutant because it fails the SUFFIX guard, not the prefix guard. The rule the reader would carry away -- 'a case that starts with the prefix cannot miss a prefix-narrowing' -- is false, and the test written from it would go green while constraining nothing. Measured today: with `startsWith(logPrefix)` narrowed to `startsWith(prefix)`, the full 742-test suite reports exactly one failure, at the `bins.delta` case, StringIndexOutOfBoundsException Range [32, 4) out of bounds for length 10 -- so the coverage is real and only the explanation of it is wrong.
